name: Prostitution (receiving fee; ordinary)
conduct: Knowingly offering or agreeing to receive a fee from another to engage in sexual conduct. This is the receiving-fee offense, not the separate paying-fee offense in §43.021. A fee can be money, goods, services or another benefit. Sexual conduct has the specific §43.01 definitions of intercourse, deviate intercourse and sexual contact; not every interaction or payment qualifies. No qualifying previous conviction under §43.02(a). It is a defense that the actor engaged in this conduct because the actor was the victim of trafficking under §20A.02 or compelling prostitution under §43.05; the causal connection to this conduct matters. For this section, a qualifying guilty/no-contest plea for deferred adjudication can count as a prior even if sentence was never imposed or probation was later discharged. The same conviction may be used for this section’s enhancement or Chapter 12 Subchapter D enhancement, but not both.
penalty: Class B misdemeanor: ordinarily up to 180 days in jail, a fine up to $2,000, or both. The paying-fee offense moved to separate §43.021 in 2021 while receiving-fee conduct remained in §43.02; earlier conduct requires the applicable historical law. Later technical amendments do not by themselves establish when a penalty first began. Other sentencing and diversion rules require separate assessment. Article 42A.515(a) requires suspension of the sentence and community supervision for the Class B offense, except when the jury assesses punishment under subsection (e); the ordinary custody maximum does not remove that requirement. When supervision is imposed under article 42A.515, participation in a commercially sexually exploited persons court program is required if one is established in the county of residence, not unconditionally statewide.

name: Solicitation of prostitution (adult first)
conduct: Knowingly offering or agreeing to pay a fee to another person for the purpose of engaging in sexual conduct with that person or another. A fee can be money, goods, services or another benefit. Sexual conduct has the specific §43.01 definitions of intercourse, deviate intercourse and sexual contact; not every interaction or payment qualifies. This branch excludes any actual, represented or believed under-18 circumstance and any qualifying prior solicitation conviction. For this section, a qualifying guilty/no-contest plea for deferred adjudication can count as a prior even if sentence was never imposed or probation was later discharged. The same conviction may be used for this section’s enhancement or Chapter 12 Subchapter D enhancement, but not both. This choice excludes the school/function/UIL proximity circumstance in §43.021(b-1), which raises the prescribed punishment by one category.
penalty: State jail felony: ordinarily 180 days to two years in state jail and a possible fine up to $10,000. The ordinary state-jail/prior-third-degree scheme began September 1, 2021, not 2025. The school/function/UIL punishment increase was enacted in 2021 and relocated to §43.021(b-1) in 2023; relocation did not first create the increase. The current minor-predicate wording was amended effective September 1, 2025. If any element predates an applicable change, the earlier law governs; charging date alone is insufficient. Other sentencing findings require separate analysis. Article 62.001(5)(B-1) uses the registration condition “punishable as a felony of the second degree,” not simply an under-18 label. School-enhanced repeat and minor cases therefore require the applicable Chapter 62 assessment; this choice does not rule registration out or assign automatic lifetime registration. A local first-offender solicitation program is optional and subject to statutory eligibility and prosecutor consent, not mandatory for every conviction.

name: Promotion of prostitution (proceeds; ordinary)
conduct: Knowingly receiving money or other property under an agreement to participate in the proceeds of prostitution. The actor must be acting other than as a person receiving compensation for personally rendered prostitution services; that excluded personal-services role is not automatically promotion. A fee can be money, goods, services or another benefit. Sexual conduct has the specific §43.01 definitions of intercourse, deviate intercourse and sexual contact; not every interaction or payment qualifies. This ordinary branch excludes a previous §43.03 conviction and conduct involving a person younger than 18.
penalty: Third-degree felony: ordinarily two to ten years in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. These promotion grades were increased effective September 1, 2019. The minor branch’s wording was broadened effective September 1, 2023; if any element predates the applicable amendment, earlier law governs. A prior is not assumed, and the deferred-adjudication rule in §43.021 is not automatically imported into this separate section. Other sentencing or registration consequences require separate assessment.

name: Continuous promotion of prostitution (two or more acts over at least 30 days)
conduct: During a period of 30 or more days, engaging two or more times in conduct constituting promotion of prostitution under §43.03. Each predicate requires its own knowing proceeds-agreement or compensated-solicitation conduct and the personal-services exclusion. A single act or a shorter period does not establish this offense. The jury need not agree on the exact predicate acts/dates, but must unanimously agree on two or more qualifying acts over the required period. The same-victim restrictions in subsections (c) and (d) limit an additional §43.03 conviction in the same case and multiple continuous-promotion counts; the statutory alternative-charge, outside-period and lesser-included exceptions remain.
penalty: First-degree felony: ordinarily five to 99 years or life in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. This offense was added effective September 1, 2025; it is not assigned to earlier conduct. This choice covers only a conduct period entirely on or after that effective date; an earlier or straddling period requires separate applicability review. Other enhancements and consequences require separate assessment.

name: Aggravated promotion of prostitution (enterprise using two or more persons)
conduct: Knowingly owning, investing in, financing, controlling, supervising or managing a prostitution enterprise that uses two or more persons engaged in prostitution. A transaction or association alone is not a substitute for the stated enterprise role and two-person requirement. Prostitution has the specific §43.02 receiving-fee meaning.
penalty: First-degree felony: ordinarily five to 99 years or life in prison and a possible fine up to $10,000. The current first-degree grade for the enterprise offense began September 1, 2019; if any element predates that amendment, earlier law governs. Registration and community-supervision restrictions require their applicable statutory analysis. Section 43.04 is expressly listed as a reportable registration conviction. Ordinary judge-ordered community supervision is excluded by article 42A.054(a)(14), with the separate victim-only finding exception in (e); jury-recommended supervision is excluded by article 42A.056(6). Deferred adjudication is a separate question with article 42A.102(b)(2) history restrictions, not a blanket promise of eligibility.
